Building an app with AI? Learn these 4 parts first Want to build an app with AI? Learn the four parts first: the front end, the back end, the database, and where AI fits in a modern app. When you ask ChatGPT or Claude to build you an app (vibe coding, no code), these four parts are what you're actually describing. Explained for complete beginners. We follow one customer message through an online coffee store app, start to finish: 1. Front end: everything the customer sees and taps. The screens, the buttons, the text box. It doesn't know prices or stock. It shows things and passes messages along. 2. Back end: runs on a server the customer never sees. This is where the business rules live: login, stock, prices, payments. The front end asks, the back end decides. 3. Database: where everything is saved, like a giant spreadsheet that never closes. Products, prices, customers, orders. Only the back end opens it, and it checks who's asking. 4. AI in the middle: the back end calls the AI model only for jobs that need understanding. Job one, turn a plain sentence ("a gift for my dad, he drinks it black, under $40") into a search. Job two, write the answer using only the real products the database sent back. The rule for building reliable AI apps: AI handles the words, the back end handles the facts and the money. Never let the AI make up prices or stock. Whole app in four lines: the front end shows, the back end decides, the database remembers, the AI understands and writes. If you want to go from understanding the four parts to building your own apps with AI, I teach it step by step, from complete beginner to real systems.
